links.outcome: Readability (FKGL) of LLM answers to patient MMF questions
links.effect: CAM readability was statistically significantly poorer (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level = 22.7 ± 12.9; P < .001); overall readability remained limited and model-dependent.
links.quote: CAM performed comparably in accuracy (86.3 ± 7.1%); however, its readability was statistically significantly poorer (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level = 22.7 ± 12.9; P < .001).

links.outcome: Hallucination (fabricated content) rate in LLM answers to MMF questions
links.effect: DOT-1 hallucination rate 5.2% vs DOT-2 10.1% and PM 9.4% (P = .013); accuracy ranged from 79.6% to 88.5%.
links.quote: It also had a statistically significantly lower hallucination rate (5.2%) compared with DOT-2 (10.1%) and PM (9.4%) (P = .013).

screen.reason: The study evaluates 5 publicly accessible LLMs on answering patient FAQs regarding maxillomandibular fixation, assessing accuracy, readability, and hallucinations without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail intervention.
